question.prompt:
Jean made a piece of stained glass art in the shape of two mountains, as shown in the figure below. One mountain peak is \(8\) feet high and the other peak is \(12\) feet high. Each peak forms a \(90^\circ\) angle, and the straight sides of the mountains form \(45^\circ\) angles with the ground. The artwork has an area of \(183\) square feet. The sides of the mountains meet at an intersection point near the center of the artwork, \(h\) feet above the ground. What is the value of \(h?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2024_AMC_8_Q24_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Extend the two inward sloping sides from their intersection down to the ground. This completes two mountain triangles. Their common region is another triangle, bounded by the ground and those two inward sides, with height \(h\).

Each completed mountain and the overlap triangle has two \(45^\circ\) base angles. Dropping a perpendicular from the top of any one of these triangles divides it into two \(45^\circ\)-\(45^\circ\)-\(90^\circ\) triangles. Equal angles have equal opposite sides, so each horizontal leg equals the height. Consequently, a triangle of height \(t\) feet has base \(2t\) feet and area
\[
\frac{1}{2}(2t)t=t^2
\]
square feet.

The completed mountains therefore have areas \(8^2=64\) and \(12^2=144\), while their overlap has area \(h^2\). Adding the two mountain areas counts the overlap twice, but the artwork contains it only once. Thus
\[
64+144-h^2=183,
\]
so
\[
h^2=208-183=25.
\]
Since a height is nonnegative, \(h=5\) feet. This is below both peaks, as required. The answer is \(\boxed{5}\), choice \(B\).
solutions.title: Complete the triangles and subtract the overlap
